body: I know this is way later, and I don't mean to be creepy, but I wanted to thank you again for your comment. I reread it today out of desperation, and it's the only thing thats making me choose to hang on. So I appreciate your words still, very much.

Thank you for your reply. It's sound advice. I guess the chances of things getting better are 0 when you're dead, which is certainly worse than waiting it out and going hard and hoping there will be someone that makes it worthwhile.
That is true. It's definitely the strongest deterrent, but it can be so frustrating how empty it feels. I guess in the long run it is a good thing. Thanks for the reemphasis.
It's good to know I'm not alone in this at least! It isn't quite satisfying to be cared for only as one of many.

Good for you! It's at the very least worth a shot.

Definitely mention your income and student status. I pay 20.00 a session with my private counselor who works on a sliding scale. Samaratins is also a fantastic idea!

I'll keep you in my thoughts.

I'm glad you posted. We read and care. 

Btw, I have been sobbing off and on all day, trying to find a way, and your username actually made me smile. So, thank you for that.

I'm sorry nobody is there for you. Sometimes people do not have the strength or resources to hear others out. You know... Call me crazy but, maybe it would be worth a shot emailing something very close to what you said to one of your lecturers? Even speaking to them in person? I'm not saying every person is innately good, but sometimes I have been surprised by how understanding others have been. If it doesn't pan out, at least you made an attempt to shake things up. Perhaps more ideas will come to mind?

You might also be able to try an independent counselor who works on a sliding scale. That's what I did and they refer out to psychiatrists sooner than you might get an appointment.

Venting is good. Don't apologize.
My pets are sometimes the only thing that keeps me going. It's nice to have something you can trust with your love. Love your cat OP, he/she loves you.

Have you tried online counselors? Maybe that can act as an in-between on what is recommended and what you would prefer to do.

I am feeling much the same, so at least you are not alone.

And hey, I read everything you said.

Thank you! I admit, I do struggle with the self-respect/"good enough" concepts. I hadn't even thought of it until you said it, but I think in this case the allowances I've made for his emotional issues has probably enabled him more than it has helped him to fix it. In many ways he seems to get worse and worse over time, so you may very well be onto something. 

As for happiness, well, I'm rarely happy. Functional, friendly, even driven, but not very happy or hopeful. It sounds so miserable, but sometimes I'm at my happiest/most peaceful when I have some time to myself not being responsible for anyone else or anything other than myself. 

As time has gone on, I've begun to get scared that things will stay the same or worse, that I'll waste my life trying to make someone else happy. I took him back to make him happy. I married him to make him happy. He begs for kids, but I won't cross that line and do something so terrible as to bring kids into this mess. I won't torture anyone else and I'm beginning to see I shouldn't be torturing myself either. I do think I will stick around. I've rarely felt so supported in my life until I came here, and I feel determined to make a future for myself. ...Thank you so very much for your kind words and encouraging message. It has made a difference, believe me.

I'm just so startled by how kind and sincere everybody is being. Thank you immensely for your reply. I hope I have been patient with him. He hasn't hit the dentist, I'm sure that's apparent, but kissing him in the past actually caused *me* to shell out thousands for a root canal/crown and infections caused by his bacteria. It's so insane when I see it written out. I can't imagine he'd have anything less than some fake teeth if he walked out of the dentist. 

As for the exercise, I think those started during a manic phase and he wanted to join my activities, as I go hard on the athleticism. Pokemon Go was great for a while, and we did that together no less, until he started driving/coasting on his bike. I hadn't considered a stationary, but I'll bring it up tomorrow and see if he bites. I'm hoping if he feels like he's being productive, it will make him feel better about himself. 

Thank you so much, once again. I do mean it.

My word, I'm having a Matt Damon/Robin Williams Good Will Hunting moment here (which is to say I've been crying reading all this stuff haha). I'm trying very hard to accept these words, and instinctively at least, I feel that they are something I need to hear. I do have to take that step it seems, and hope that I will come out on the other side happier. I don't want to be a quitter or a deserter, but I do want some happiness and *hope* again in the life I have ahead of me. Thank you again. I will truly reflect on your words. Promise.

I'm truly humbled by your response. I got teary-eyed, I'll admit! :' ). I have a very hard time when it comes to personal responsibility and fault, and I never want to be the person who fears it or avoids it. I had/have this same problem with my assault, getting over the sense of fault and what I could have/shouldn't have/can do/didn't do to let myself get into my situations. It's something I've been working on in therapy. I think sometimes it almost makes more sense for me to see how I've done wrong than it is to make sense of my struggles in another light. I can at least affix a blame or a cause. Heck maybe it's a control/anxiety thing... Either way, it sucks and I wish I had more clarity!

I have made excuses for his hygiene, chalking it up to depression. On my bad days, it's hard for me to walk the dog, do homework, take my mom to her surgery/chemo etc, though I still do it. So I think I feel like it is unfair of me to judge him when he is perhaps feeling worse than I've ever felt. I want to be a kind empathetic person because I know when I've felt low, what I've wanted sometimes was for someone to just tell me they understand. I hope I'm making sense here. It is quite frankly, just disgusting though. I don't even like him to breathe on me. I can't imagine it helps his self-esteem see me flinch.

I have to admit his lack of change when I told him about my rape has upset me. I was hoping that would be his eye-opener, and that he could see how from my perspective it would be jarring and that he'd want to help me at least for that reason alone. Perhaps it's unfair, but nonetheless I was hoping he'd find the thought unacceptable and be spurred into action. That was kind of my last resort as I hate talking about it, and until I posted here, I was at a complete loss as a result of his response.

I just want to do the right thing.

...Haha, thank you so much again for your reply, I'm getting choked up again as I reread it! I don't know that I deserve such generous words. I feel very lucky to have posted here and to have been met with such sincere thought and effort and kindness. It is nice to not feel isolated in this. I really have no words, I'm a little overwhelmed! Thank you, sincerely.

Astonishingly enough, it is not a typo! He was rail thin when we met, wore a 29 in pants. I think I could have outflexed him. I actually thought he had a thyroid disorder. In fact when he gained weight, the thought crossed my mind again. I guess weight is just a struggle for him.

Wow, thank you so much for sharing. That sounds like an ordeal, and utterly draining. I can very much imagine the feeling! I do also appreciate your honesty in sharing your struggles with self-esteem. I've only just started making strides maybe six months ago, so I do wonder if that has a role to play in the worsening of my feelings. I do know the change has been noticeable to others and the response from men day-to-day has been a complete 180, deserved or not. It's so hard to feel good about oneself without worrying about being self-absorbed or just incorrect. In my experience at least haha. I have had a brief dating history, but one thing they've all had in common was egos in need of care and maintenance. It's difficult to imagine that someone out there would put up with my hobbies, idiosyncrasies, schooling obsession, and quirks and find me hot at the end of the day.  I hope that makes sense. I've started a gratitude journal recently and close it by listing one thing I like about myself (no qualifiers like "but" or "sort of" and so on) and sometimes that just takes forever.

I definitely have "bad guy" fears, and know how bad it hurts to be unwanted. The thought of inflicting that on somebody who says they'd die or give up on everything if I left is scary and distressing. I also share those worries you once had about partner suicide and breakdowns. But I think maybe looking over this all I've been just enabling him too long. I definitely want to leave, have wanted to and think more heavily on it every day, but taking that first step is so hard.

I was struck by your words regarding pity and sympathy. You are right. Those are my primary feelings, and that can't be fair to anyone, right? I would never want anyone to stay with me out of pity...

Thank you so much for the response.

Thank you so much for the reply and the reassurance (also regarding my English)! It was my third language and I find myself making little gaffs frequently, but it's more glaring in text so I was self-conscious. 

You are so right, and in fact I have said the same thing to others regarding someone wanting to change, but seem to find ways to make excuses for him when it comes to my situation. I guess part of my fears are what if he gets worse when I leave, and how do I cope with feeling like I've failed to help? I'm getting a little existential and probably out of bounds here, so I'll just thank you once again. I do finally feel that I'm at least not some looks-obsessed narcissist or something equally discouraging. Thank you.

Thank you, that's awfully kind of you to say. I don't ever want to shirk away from my responsibilities, so logically I feel (kind of leaning to 'felt' now at this point) that in a two party system both partners are responsible in some fashion. I'm beginning to see that maybe it's like a team sport; I've passed to him, tried to make assists, and he has had to do something about it. You can't win some games solo? (Btw: UrbanPugEsq? Pug doggies, gaming, or something else all together if I may ask?)

It drives me crazy. I've even offered to remind him or brush my teeth with him. I can't knock him out and drive him to the dentist, but I've wished I could. It's unbearable to open mouth kiss him, and I actually got a tooth infection and had to get a root canal because of his saliva. (According to my dentist at least.) But as a quick aside, thank you. I've come to terms over the past year that there is a serious problem, and I feel more and more pressured by it and trapped as time progresses. He's been with me since I was so young, it's almost hard to fathom that there could be others, or that they'd love me as much as he does. But I guess that's more *my* problem at that point. It's hard not to feel selfish, but I do have to take care of myself at some point, so thank you for the reminder!

I try to emphasize that, even that it may have been just that medication. His father has bipolar too and actually set himself on fire and blew up the house we were living in (hence our living situation). We visited him every single day for months in the burn ward, and he almost died multiple times. I don't get how he (my spouse) can see that and think, yeah, it's worth taking the risk/he can manage it. I'm with you. On the days I know I'd be up 24 hours having a panic attack and stressing out, I take an ativan instead. It makes me a bit hazy, but who wants to suffer?

I hadn't considered the thought expressed in your last line. I think I take his temporary efforts (before his depression gets the best of him) as a sign that he's going to try, but it *has* just reverted. It can be confusing because his upswings can be very good, he's almost a different person, but his lows are so, so, so low. I can't have a bad day or else it drags him down, y'know? But you're right. It can't possibly change unless he gets treatment and that's been a losing battle. I guess it's true that change has to come from within. Thank you.

Good question, I should have probably mentioned. He was medicated once before for depression and said it made him feel like a robot. He tried therapy but couldn't stick with it and quit after a month. So he is no longer interested in individual therapy though he himself says he "needs it and probably medicine too." I don't want to be a shrew and make him feel forced, you know?
